objective: Prove GPTQueue agent communication across the full lifecycle - distinct registration and readiness, 1-to-1, 1-to-N, and 3x2 complete-bipartite delivery with exact payload, sender attribution, no missing edges, no duplicate logical delivery, and no cross-delivery; retry idempotency via idempotency keys; stateless process continuity through session re-binding; stale transport recovery; graceful close versus terminal unregister with registration, mailbox, lease, and transport-session cleanup back to baseline; typed observable backpressure refusal; and concurrent interleaving of a 2x3 complete bipartite matrix where two senders transmit concurrently via Promise.all over ordinary send_message calls, proving interleaved sends still yield exactly six unique edges with correct attribution and zero duplicates or cross-delivery, and restart durability where a message accepted as sent immediately before a real server SIGKILL and respawn remains receivable afterward through session re-binding - through bounded deterministic scenarios executed by a Node runner inside the MetaBuilder sandbox over a Unix-domain-socket HTTP MCP transport with an in-sandbox Unix-socket redis-server, without any live server, live Redis db0, network egress, or target-source writes.

requirements.statement: [H1][H2][H3][H4] Every actor in each scenario receives a distinct usable session identity, appears through list_agents, and passes an explicit readiness barrier before any sender transmits; one registered sender delivers one correlated message to exactly one registered receiver with exact payload and sender attribution; one sender fans out over N ordinary send_message calls so every intended receiver gets exactly one edge and no other actor gets one; and the deterministic 3x2 complete bipartite matrix yields six uniquely identified edges where each receiver gets exactly three messages with complete sender attribution, no missing edges, no duplicate logical delivery, and no cross-delivery, across at least three consecutive bounded rounds.
acceptance: harness/lifecycle/run-scenario.mjs topology --rounds 3 exits zero inside the sandboxed adapter for three consecutive rounds, and its result summary reports for each round: distinct session ids per actor, list_agents containing every registered actor, a readiness barrier pass, the 1-to-1 edge delivered with exact payload and matching sender attribution, exactly N fan-out send_message calls producing exactly the N expected edges, and the 3x2 matrix producing exactly six unique edges with each receiver observing exactly three messages attributed to all three senders.

The result summary reports zero missing edges, zero duplicate logical deliveries, and zero cross-deliveries for every round; correlation is by scenario id, round id, sender, receiver, and unique per-edge idempotency key.

requirements.statement: [H5] Repeating an edge with the same idempotency key does not create a second logical delivery, while distinct edge keys remain distinct.
acceptance: harness/lifecycle/run-scenario.mjs idempotency --rounds 3 exits zero and its result summary reports, per round: re-sending one edge with the identical idempotency key yields the original message id and the receiver observes exactly one logical delivery for that key, while a distinct key on the same sender-receiver pair yields a separate logical delivery. Correlation is by scenario id, round id, sender, receiver, and unique per-edge idempotency key.

requirements.statement: [H6][H7] A replacement client process resumes an existing registered session by passing the retained session_id to a session-scoped tool without re-registering, and receives an already queued message; a stale HTTP transport session id is rejected through the documented error response, re-initialization on the same transport succeeds, and subsequent messaging is valid.
acceptance: harness/lifecycle/run-scenario.mjs continuity --rounds 3 exits zero and its result summary reports, per round: after a queued message, a fresh transport connection calling receive_message with only the retained session_id receives the queued message without re-registration; and after a server-side transport-session invalidation, a tools/call with the stale mcp-session id is refused with the documented 404 response whose body reports the session-expired error and directs re-initialization, a fresh initialize on the same endpoint succeeds, and a subsequent send/receive exchange is delivered with correct attribution. Correlation is by scenario id, round id, sender, receiver, and unique per-edge idempotency key.

requirements.statement: [H8] Graceful close_session and terminal unregister_agent have their distinct documented semantics - close preserves the queued mailbox and stops lease refresh while unregister removes registration and mailbox state - and after all test-owned actors terminate, the isolated server reports no leftover registrations and its health session count returns to the recorded baseline.
acceptance: harness/lifecycle/run-scenario.mjs cleanup --rounds 3 exits zero and its result summary reports, per round: close_session returns session_closed with mailbox preserved and the closed session id is refused by a subsequent session-scoped call returning the documented session-unavailable error rather than any generic error (evidencing the closed session's lease record is absent and lease refresh has stopped); after unregister_agent the agent no longer appears in list_agents, a session-scoped call with its session_id is refused, and a message sent to the unregistered agent is refused; and the server /health session count equals the recorded pre-scenario baseline after every test-owned actor has exited.

The result summary reports no surviving transport-session state for any test-owned actor; no surviving registration or mailbox state for terminally unregistered actors; and gracefully closed actors retain exactly their documented registry and mailbox state with lease refresh stopped (no lease key refresh activity after close).

requirements.statement: [H9] The bounded queue refusal is observable and typed, never silent message loss: when the receiver's bounded queue is at capacity, further sends are refused through the documented typed error while earlier queued messages remain receivable.
acceptance: harness/lifecycle/run-scenario.mjs backpressure --rounds 3 exits zero and its result summary reports, per round: with GPTQ_QUEUE_BOUND set small, sends beyond the bound return the documented typed queue-full error, zero messages are lost silently, every message queued before the refusals is subsequently received intact with correct sender attribution and its per-edge idempotency key, and after the receiver drains, a subsequent send with a fresh idempotency key is delivered.

requirements.statement: [H10] The deterministic 2x3 complete bipartite matrix survives concurrent interleaving: when the two senders transmit their three edges each concurrently (for example Promise.all over the ordinary send_message calls, no ordering assumptions), the scenario still yields exactly six unique edges with complete sender attribution and per-receiver receiver observations of exactly two messages, zero missing edges, zero duplicate logical deliveries, and zero cross-deliveries, across three consecutive bounded rounds.
acceptance: harness/lifecycle/run-scenario.mjs concurrent --rounds 3 exits zero inside the sandboxed adapter for three consecutive rounds, and its result summary reports for each round: the two senders' six send_message calls issued concurrently (Promise.all or equivalent) with no assumed delivery ordering, yielding exactly six unique edges where each of the three receivers observes exactly two messages, exactly one attributed to each sender, and zero duplicate logical deliveries and zero cross-deliveries. Correlation is by scenario id, round id, sender, receiver, and unique per-edge idempotency key.

The result summary reports zero missing edges for every round; the concurrent send results are not ordered, sequenced, or serialized by the scenario; every edge is matched purely by its idempotency key and attribution, never by arrival order.

requirements.statement: [H11] A message accepted by the server (send_message returned its sent result) immediately before a real server SIGKILL and respawn is still receivable afterward by a client process re-binding the retained session_id on a fresh transport connection, across three consecutive bounded rounds.
acceptance: harness/lifecycle/run-scenario.mjs restart --rounds 3 exits zero inside the sandboxed adapter for three consecutive rounds, and its result summary reports for each round: a sender's message was accepted (sent result observed) immediately before the runner killed the HTTP server with SIGKILL and respawned it against the same in-sandbox redis-server (whose data store survives the kill), after which a fresh client process re-binding the retained receiver session_id (without re-registering) received that exact message with correct sender attribution and its per-edge idempotency key. Correlation is by scenario id, round id, sender, receiver, and unique per-edge idempotency key.

The result summary reports that no re-registration occurred for the re-bound session, the message content survived the kill byte-for-byte, and the respawned server was a genuinely fresh process (new pid, health observed before the re-bind).

requirements.statement: The committed TypeScript target typechecks without emit on the current host.
acceptance: tsc --noEmit over the committed tsconfig.json exits zero inside the sandboxed adapter with no filesystem writes to the target workspace.

epoch.intent: Review the communication-lifecycle epoch: what the topology, idempotency, continuity, cleanup, and backpressure scenarios observed, which invariants held or failed, what product or model defects were exposed, and the next bounded improvement or convergence decision.
